Where Education Connects With Industry

Knowledge becomes powerful when it meets experience.

At Pradako Mechanical & Engineering Works, we believe the strongest careers are built when academic knowledge is supported by meaningful industry exposure.

Through our Academic and Institutional Partnerships Programme, we welcome colleges, universities, polytechnic institutes, Industrial Training Institutes, vocational centres, professional academies, coaching institutions and skill-development organisations.

Whether an institution is seeking a focused engagement or a long-term academic alliance, we are open to partnerships that create meaningful value for students, educators and industry.

∞

Learning does not end with a qualification. It begins wherever curiosity meets opportunity.

01

OPENING THE DOORS TO INDUSTRY

Industrial Visits

Educational institutions may apply to organise structured industrial visits for students, faculty members or academic delegations. The experience is designed to reveal how departments, systems, processes and people work together inside a modern industrial organisation.

POSSIBLE EXPOSURE

  • Manufacturing and production operations
  • Quality assurance and inspection
  • Planning and process coordination
  • Supply chain and procurement
  • Warehousing and logistics
  • Maintenance and utilities
  • Human resources and administration
  • Sales and customer coordination
  • Export and international business
  • Workplace safety and compliance
  • Sustainability and responsible manufacturing

VISIT FORMATS

  • Student groups
  • Faculty delegations
  • Departmental batches
  • Academic orientation programmes
  • Career-awareness initiatives
  • Project-based learning groups
  • Industry-readiness programmes

The purpose is not only to observe production activity. It is to understand discipline, teamwork, planning, quality, communication, responsibility and continuous improvement. Requests are reviewed against academic relevance, group size, preferred dates, operational availability and safety requirements.

02

FROM CLASSROOM LEARNING TO WORKPLACE CONFIDENCE

Internships & Industrial Training

Pradako welcomes internship and industrial training requests from recognised educational institutions and eligible students. Programmes are intended to build practical exposure, workplace awareness and a clearer understanding of professional responsibility.

WHO MAY APPLY

  • Undergraduate and postgraduate students
  • Diploma students and ITI trainees
  • Vocational learners
  • Management students
  • Commerce and finance students
  • Information technology students
  • Marketing and communication students
  • Supply chain and logistics students
  • Other relevant academic disciplines

PROGRAMME OPTIONS

  • Compulsory academic internships
  • Voluntary internships
  • Summer and winter internships
  • Short-term industrial training
  • Semester-based internships
  • Final-year projects
  • Departmental training programmes
  • Research-oriented assignments
  • Faculty-supported projects
  • Practical exposure programmes

THE LEARNING JOURNEY

  • Organisational orientation
  • Departmental exposure
  • Defined assignments or projects
  • Guidance from experienced professionals
  • Workplace communication and conduct
  • Quality, productivity and safety awareness
  • Periodic reviews and feedback
  • Practical documentation
  • Final presentation or learning summary

Every request is reviewed according to academic background, area of interest, duration, institutional requirements and the availability of suitable supervision. Submission does not automatically guarantee a placement.

03

BUILDING CAREER-READY GRADUATES

Fresher Opportunities

We are committed to identifying, welcoming and developing promising young talent. Institutions may introduce suitable graduating students and recent graduates for entry-level opportunities across multiple areas of the organisation.

POTENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Production and operations
  • Quality and inspection
  • Technical support
  • Planning and coordination
  • Supply chain and procurement
  • Warehousing and logistics
  • Sales and business development
  • Export and international business
  • Finance and accounts
  • Human resources
  • Information technology
  • Administration
  • Marketing and communication
  • Sustainability and compliance
  • Customer coordination
  • Management support functions

WHAT WE VALUE

  • Willingness to learn
  • Professional discipline
  • Integrity and responsibility
  • Curiosity and initiative
  • Clear communication
  • Teamwork and respect
  • Adaptability
  • Attention to quality
  • A positive approach to continuous improvement

Fresher opportunities are not limited to technical qualifications. Candidates from different academic backgrounds may be considered according to role suitability and organisational requirements.

04

CONNECTING TALENT WITH OPPORTUNITY

Campus Recruitment & Job Placements

We welcome placement cells, Training and Placement Officers, career-development departments and institutional representatives interested in exploring campus recruitment partnerships with Pradako.

ENGAGEMENTS MAY INCLUDE

  • Pre-placement presentations
  • Company orientation sessions
  • Industry and career-awareness programmes
  • Aptitude or functional assessments
  • Role-based evaluations
  • Group interactions
  • Personal interviews
  • Department-specific recruitment drives
  • Graduate trainee opportunities
  • Management trainee opportunities
  • Internship-to-employment pathways
  • Pooled campus recruitment drives
  • Multi-institution recruitment programmes

INSTITUTIONS MAY SHARE

  • Placement calendars
  • Course and specialisation details
  • Student profiles
  • Graduation timelines
  • Batch strength
  • Location preferences
  • Eligibility information
  • Available campus facilities
  • Proposed recruitment dates

Our objective is to support a transparent and structured recruitment process that helps students understand opportunities while enabling Pradako to identify candidates aligned with our values, culture and future requirements.

05

ENGAGEMENT BEYOND PLACEMENTS

Campus Connect Programmes

Industry engagement should begin before the final year. Campus Connect helps students understand career possibilities, professional expectations and the practical relevance of academic learning.

PROGRAMME THEMES

  • Industry-awareness sessions
  • Career-readiness workshops
  • Workplace-expectation programmes
  • Resume and interview preparation
  • Professional communication sessions
  • Manufacturing and business case studies
  • Quality and productivity awareness
  • Leadership and teamwork discussions
  • Supply chain and business-process awareness
  • International business and export orientation
  • Sustainability and responsible-industry sessions
  • Entrepreneurship and innovation interactions
  • Project presentations and reviews
  • Student competitions
  • Employability-development programmes

DELIVERY MODES

  • At the educational institution
  • At a Pradako facility
  • Online
  • Through webinars
  • Through panel discussions
  • As part of a larger academic or career event

The subject, depth and format can be adapted to the academic level, area of study and intended outcome of the institution.

SUPPORTING THE EDUCATORS WHO SHAPE FUTURE TALENT

Faculty Development & Industry Immersion

POSSIBLE ENGAGEMENTS

  • Quality and productivity discussions
  • Curriculum input sessions
  • Faculty interaction with functional leaders
  • Industry case-study development
  • Joint workshops
  • Research discussions
  • Train-the-trainer programmes
  • Faculty participation in industry events

These initiatives can help educators bring practical industry context into classrooms, projects and student-development programmes.

  • Leadership and teamwork
  • Preparing for interviews and campus recruitment

  • Entrepreneurship and business leadership
  • Women in manufacturing and leadership

  • The future of industry and digital transformation

Sessions can be customised around academic programmes, student interests and event objectives.

How the Collaboration Process Works

Simple to begin. Structured to create value.

01

Submit Your Request

Complete the Academic and Institutional Partnership Form or send your proposal by email.

02

Internal Review

We review the objective, relevance, dates, participant profile and operational feasibility.

03

Programme Discussion

Suitable proposals move into a discussion on scope, format, schedule, responsibilities and outcomes.

04

Confirmation & Coordination

The approved programme is coordinated with the authorised institutional representative.

05

Engagement & Outcomes

The visit, recruitment activity, session, training or partnership is delivered according to the agreed plan.

Important Application Guidelines

Clear expectations create better experiences.

Requests should preferably be submitted through an authorised institutional representative, placement officer, faculty coordinator or official institutional email address.

Institutions should provide adequate notice before the preferred engagement date. Lead time helps us evaluate operational availability, safety, supervision and internal coordination.

Group sizes may be limited according to safety and supervision. Production or restricted areas may require specific internal approvals. Photography, videography and recording may also be restricted.

No. Internship and employment opportunities depend on current organisational requirements, suitable supervision and role availability. Campus recruitment participation does not guarantee selection or employment.

Confidential business, technical and customer information will not be shared. Confirmed participants may be required to follow confidentiality, safety and professional-conduct guidelines.

Final approval for any engagement remains subject to operational feasibility, internal review and company policy.

Apply for a Partnership

Tell us what you want to create.
